VBO:0200673.summary: Character varies across the hound family: the Beagle is merry and determined, while the Whippet is gentle, affectionate and even-tempered. Their shared heritage is hunting, with scent hounds following trails by nose and sight hounds such as the Whippet relying on vision and speed. Some members add a distinctive bay to their pursuit.
VBO:0200673.shortDescription: With character ranging from merry Beagles to gentle Whippets, hounds unite scent-trailing and swift visual hunters.

sources.title: American Kennel Club — Hound Group
sources.evidence: Actual complete substantive introductory paragraph read: most hounds share hunting heritage; some follow a scent trail, others use stamina in pursuit; very diverse examples and hard generalizations; baying only some. Initial displayed named breed summaries read, not every site-linked breed article. No universal hound temperament or exhaustive worldwide membership inferred.

sources.title: National Bluetick Coonhound Association — AKC club flyer
sources.evidence: Actual entire two-page national-club flyer read. Explicit scent-hound versus sight-hound family distinction: Whippet and Greyhound use eyesight and speed, Beagle and Bloodhound follow nose; Bluetick is one scent member. Bluetick-specific affection/charm/prey drive not generalized or used as Whippet temperament.

sources.title: FCI Standard162 — Whippet
sources.evidence: Actual entire five-page 2019 English standard read. Whippet gentle, affectionate and even disposition; balanced muscular elegance and speed, long lean head, black nose, oval eyes, fine small rose ears, arching neck/loin, deep brisket/tuck, straight moderate forelegs, muscular hindquarters, oval feet, smooth fine coat and long tapering unfeathered delicate-curved tail. Male47–51cm. All anatomy belongs only to the pictured Whippet representative.

sources.title: FCI Standard161 — Beagle
sources.evidence: Actual entire six-page English standard read. Named Beagle merry, bold, enduring/determined, alert, intelligent and even/amiable; historic hare pack work. Normative whole head/body/limbs/coat/tail read to distinguish it from Whippet, not blended into representative anatomy.
